Why rich people never say "I can't afford it."

Kevin explains a small mental switch: cancel that sentence and say, "I can't afford that right now, but I will." He says the feeling behind it is what matters.

Then he gets practical. Online shops, local marketplaces and estate sales make it easy to pick up a small trinket from a grand house for next to nothing. In his view, that little item carries the same energy as the big chandelier from the same house.

What would you start collecting if cost didn't hold you back?

#ad #money #mindset #wealth

Why would a wealthy person keep a very old book at home?

Kevin explains that the older the better, because it has passed through the hands of monks and enlightened beings. In his view, an object like that has a resonance, and wealthy people want it in their space.

He says that walking past it every day shapes you, and that you become a magnet for the things you want yourself.

What objects around you remind you of who you want to become?

#ad #wealth #habits #mindset

He built a castle just to hold his obsession.

Kevin tells the story of William Randolph Hearst, one of the richest men in America at the time, and his home at San Simeon in California. The movie Citizen Kane was technically about him.

Kevin has visited several times. He says Hearst was obsessed with art, especially sculpture, and travelled the world collecting ancient, priceless marble pieces to fill the place.

What do you love so much that you would surround yourself with it?
